added: Oblada updates itself: once a day it looks for a new version, downloads it in the background and installs it when you quit, or right away from About Oblada's Relaunch button. Your tabs come back after the relaunch.
Before importing passwords from another browser, Oblada tells you macOS will ask for your Mac's password.
fixed: On a Mac with another Chromium-based browser, Oblada no longer asks for your password when it first opens: it keeps its own key in the Keychain.
knownIssues: After each update, macOS asks once for your Mac's password before Oblada can read its saved passwords and cookies.
notes: Updates are signed: Oblada installs only versions signed by its developers, and checks them before unpacking them.
This version still has to be installed by hand, as before; the next ones arrive on their own.
If you used an earlier version, you'll have to sign in to websites again, and passwords saved in Oblada can't be read anymore: Oblada's key for them changed.
